codeReview.summary: APP-003 implements the Second Exec Login Entry test case with comprehensive crash signature capture. The implementation correctly extends the ios_app_harness.c with test_app_003() function that launches the iOS app, captures simulator logs, extracts boot milestones, detects crash indicators, generates normalized crash signatures, and writes all required JSON artifacts. The Meson wiring is complete and follows the established pattern from previous APP cases.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The test_app_003() function follows a consistent 7-step pattern seen in other APP test functions: (1) Launch app, (2) Capture logs, (3) Extract milestones, (4) Check crash indicators, (5) Generate crash signature, (6) Write artifacts, (7) Verify success criteria. This pattern is not documented in AGENTS.md but workers have correctly replicated it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: ios_app_harness.c:2015-2420 - test_app_003() implementation showing the consistent 7-step structure matching test_app_001() and test_app_002()

sharedStateObservations.observation: The crash signature normalizer uses a deterministic hash algorithm (normalized_hash_v1) that combines crash_type, exception_code, faulting_pc, and milestone_context. This is consistent with APPSIM-005 implementation and produces reproducible signatures for crash deduplication.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: ios_app_harness.c:1041-1072 - generate_crash_hash() implementation and ios_app_harness.c:2384-2405 - crash_signature.json output with algorithm field set to 'normalized_hash_v1'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The implementation correctly handles the milestone-first crash reduction approach documented in the case.yaml notes. The test may pass even if second_execve_started is not reached, allowing it to be used for crash analysis with meaningful highest_completed_milestone and first_failing_milestone data.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: case.yaml notes section: 'MAY initially classify as REAL FAIL (this is expected)' and test_app_003() line 2414 comment: 'The second_execve_started milestone is tracked but the case may pass without it'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The harness uses xcrun simctl commands directly rather than the XcodeBuildMCP tools. While this works, it bypasses the higher-level abstraction that provides better error handling and logging integration.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: ios_app_harness.c:2036 - 'xcrun simctl bootstatus', ios_app_harness.c:2042 - 'xcrun simctl launch', ios_app_harness.c:2086 - 'xcrun simctl spawn' - all direct shell commands rather than XcodeBuildMCP tool invocations

sharedStateObservations.observation: The app_boot_milestones array is defined once at line 1445 and used across all APP test functions. This shared state enables consistent milestone tracking but is not documented in any library file. Workers discovered this pattern through code reading.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: ios_app_harness.c:1445-1457 - app_boot_milestones definition with 10 milestones from app_launched to shell_ready, referenced in test_app_001 (line 1565), test_app_002 (line 1843), test_app_003 (line 2120)

summary: APP-003 implementation is complete and correct. The test case successfully captures second execve (/bin/login) entry point data with full crash signature support. All four required artifacts are generated (sim_launch.json, boot_milestones.json, second_exec.json, crash_signature.json) with the correct structure per the validation contract. The crash signature includes the required fields: highest_completed_milestone, first_failing_milestone, and normalized_signature_hash. The implementation follows established patterns from previous APP cases and includes proper Meson wiring. No blocking or non-blocking issues identified.
